answer: Because the nectar index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the copper audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 35 aliases hence needs 35 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a meadow index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
